linguistics.meaning: Ewok — borrowed English (Star Wars) name for a forest‑dweller, used as a trail nickname. No Plains Cree equivalent has been assigned to this sign.

morphemes.gloss: English‑only borrowing. Coined by George Lucas for the 1983 film Return of the Jedi; the small hooded forest‑dwelling species of Endor. Used on this trail as a builder's nickname for a tight, low, twisty forest section — the kind of trail where you ride hunched over like an Ewok through the trees. No Plains Cree translation has been carved onto the plaque, and no nêhiyawêwin calque is proposed here: the sign exists in English only, mirroring how slinky is treated elsewhere in this catalogue.

relatedForms.english: Tight, twisty singletrack section (in MTB vernacular)

morphemes.gloss: English MTB term — what 'Ewok' is doing semantically on the trail: it describes a forest section so dense and low‑clearance you feel like a small forest creature picking your way through.

relatedForms.note: Other Star‑Wars‑adjacent trail nicknames in MTB networks include 'Wookiee', 'Endor', 'Tatooine' (rough, sandy section), 'Jedi'. None are loanwords into Cree; they live as English‑vernacular only.

relatedForms.english: A small forest‑being / 'little person' (general Cree concept, not the trail name)

morphemes.gloss: Plains Cree NA noun (plural): memekwêsiwak — 'little people / small forest beings' in Plains Cree oral tradition (after Wolvengrey's memekwêsiw). Singular: memekwêsiw. Included here only to point at the nearest cultural analogue to the Ewok concept; the plaque itself carries no Cree.

relatedForms.note: Cultural reference, NOT a translation of 'Ewok'. The carved plaque is English‑only — if the community ever wanted a Cree name, memekwêsiw 'little forest being' would be one starting point, but this would need elder review before any plaque carving.

culturalStory.heading: Why no Cree?
body: Most of the plaques on this wall pair an English MTB trail name with a carved Plains Cree calque — sometimes a careful translation, sometimes a riff. The Ewok plaque is one of two on the wall (along with slinky) that does not carry a Cree headline. The design source in the ewok/ folder is a hooded forest‑creature silhouette inspired by the Endor‑dwelling Ewoks of Return of the Jedi, and the trail itself appears to be a short, tight, low‑clearance forest section — the kind of trail where the rider hunches small to fit through, the way an Ewok moves through the trees of Endor.

The catalogue mirrors the plaque: creeName is the placeholder string ewok and creeSyllabics is empty. We are not inventing a Cree name here — that would put words in the carvers' hands they did not choose to carve. If a Cree name is added later (the natural cultural analogue would be something built from memekwêsiw 'little forest being'), the page can be re‑drafted and the plaque eventually re‑carved. Until then, this page stays English‑only and points at the missing piece honestly.

Like every other sign on the wall, the trail still sits on ᓀᐦᐃᔭᐤ ᐊᐢᑭᕀ Nêhiyaw‑Askiy (Plains Cree territory). The land underneath an English name is the same land — naming the missing translation is itself part of the work.

notes: NO CREE ON THE WALL: The plaque does not appear on the visible wall photo (allSigns.jpg). The two screenshots in the ewok/ folder are design sources, not photos of a mounted plaque — the sign was likely never installed, or is on a section of the wall not in this image. Treat like slinky: English‑only, light single‑row primary section, no invented Cree.

Catalogue currently has creeName='ewok' (placeholder) and creeSyllabics='' — leave those alone for this batch. The coordinator should NOT auto‑populate a Cree name here without elder review. The brief explicitly says (see sign_inventory.md) 'leave empty or keep ewok' for this row.

Image asset: docs/assets/ewok/ewok_render.png is the original 'Screenshot 2023-12-11 at 7.14.23 PM.png' from the ewok/ folder, copied verbatim under a clean name. It is the design source for the printed plaque even though the plaque is not visible on the wall.

Trailforks: searched the Edmonton region directory and a generic 'ewok mountain bike trail Edmonton' query; no match found. Set trailforks = { notes: ... } per the brief's option‑B pattern for no‑match signs.

If/when a Cree calque is later added by the community, the obvious morphological scaffolding is memekwêsiw 'little forest being' (NA, Plains Cree oral tradition; cf. Wolvengrey). NOT carving that on the page now, only flagging it for future consideration.

Primary section has a single morpheme row (acceptance criterion: morphemes.length >= 1), mirroring the brief's instruction for English‑vernacular signs. relatedForms has 2 rows (>=1). quickReference has 3 rows (>=3). All keys are unique within the page.
